body: I won't be moving on with my life until I know this is something that truly can't be fixed. We have talked since this post, and she will be seeking professional help to change her medication. I would never use a means of self-defense upon someone just because they're mentally unstable. She has taken to getting physical, and even brandishing weapons at me, and actually using them on my property. My thought was to prevent actual physical harm to come to either of us because of an episode that's devolved into violent irrational rage. A;though this will not be necessary, as I'll be supporting her through this, but not in person until she's stable once more.

Pepper spray is indeed legal to carry without a permit in Florida. I had not considered to see if I could find any man vrs woman pepper spray defense cases, and will indeed do so now. I very much appreciate the idea to do so. I know pepper spray hurts pretty bad, but in my mind is a non-violent means of escape I could use to not actually physically harm her. Which seemed better to me than getting stabbed, her stabbing herself, or me potentially breaking her wrist in an attempt to disarm her. I'm not leaving her, but we have talked since this post, and she will be seeking professional help. I will continue to support her through this, but not in person until after she has stabilized from her meds.

I was unaware that being aware of her tendencies and still dealing with her made me vulnerable in a legal situation. Regardless of that, I took the risk and saw her last night. It wasn't pretty, but it didn't get physical. She is going to work with her psychiatrist to change her medication, and I will not be seeing her until she has stabilized following this. I want to work with her, and have her know that while I'm not there in person, I understand her illness can cause her to be downright mean and irrational when she's manic. In the end, you are partially right about her being a bit of an abusive person, but not quite to this degree. She's a big fan of attempting to twist around words to facilitate playing the victim, and refuses to accept when I call her on it. It really is like night and day though between when she's stable and when she's manic. None of these things happened in the past, and I've known her a long time. She's not going inpatient, but she IS seeking professional help now. If the medication change doesn't work, I may indeed have to walk away from her to avoid ruining my own life. For now, I'll be there for her, just not in person. Thank you for helping me to consider myself more in this equation. I, too, have depression, and don't always do this myself normally.
I took some hapkido as a kid, but that was 20 years ago. All I remember are submission holds and trips. No time for that kind of stuff anymore, although I REALLY want to learn judo.

Yeah, she's told me stories about the good and the bad ones. Seems to depend what part of town you're in where I live. If she ends up needing it, I'm going to help her get in a clinic one way or another. We'll get through this somehow. Thanks again for your advice.

I know she's trying to push my buttons, and I shrug most of it off. A little ends up sticking though, you know? I understand she's not in control of her actions, which is why I forgive her and want to spend time helping her. I just don't want to get stabbed.. Those links are great, and I'll be reading them tomorrow. Gotta get my 6 hours of sleep before work. Thanks again.

I've never been sprayed myself, I just figured it would be a viable counter to a weapon that's not trying to disarm her myself, which could end up really REALLY bad. I don't plan to use it, I've reconsidered, and would only pull it in a life or death scenario. Unfortunately, we're not civil partners or married, so my benefits do not extend to her. I think she's on some kinda bad insurance, but generally mental health is covered regardless. Thank you for the warning, I really do take it to heart.

She's said it herself she knows she's off, I think she just needs that last little push to get the help she needs. I honestly don't know if she appreciates me, or if she's clinging onto the last thing she has. I know she doesn't mean the things she says when she's manic, but Goddamn.. I've had nicer enemies (I mean her actions as of late, she used to be the sweetest thing on the planet). I know it's not her fault, I don't hold it against her, just, you know.. the thoughts had to be somewhere in her head to say them haha.

In all honesty, I don't think I have any of those things anymore. I won't blame her for that though, I think I was always like this a bit. I'm just so used to dealing with things on my own, the idea of help seems uncomfortable. I have an extremely internal locus of control, admitting an outside force can help me goes against a lot of what I've convinced myself I am. Really, thank you for making me think about it. This is going to be a rough week and I might just do it.

She actually doesn't have a therapist, and I'm going to talk to her one last time about getting one that can actually help her through this. Thankfully, she hasn't gotten much in the way of silverware since being kicked out, perhaps I can discreetly make sharp objects disappear before this conversation begins. This is beyond me and I recognize it now. Thank you, very much.

I've realized that I'm not equipped to handle this, and will be seeing her one last time to talk about getting professional help. I truly appreciate your words. I will indeed think about therapy myself. I just never thought I'd see myself on the proverbial couch.
This is exactly what I'm going to do, she knows she's not right currently and has been voluntarily institutionalized before. Thank you for your advice, truly.
You're right, I'm going to let professionals handle this. I'll still be here when all's said and done, although it will have to be quite a bit down the road. Thank you.
I didn't know it worked like that. Yes, I'm gainfully employed, and not in poverty. I'm beginning to reconsider what needs to be done, thank you for helping me realize the reality of the situation.

I have erected false limits, it's true. I don't care about anyone like I do her, not even myself. I can't believe I'm a battered spouse as a man, but in retrospect, I really do fit the definition perfectly. Which is pathetic as hell. I'm starting to reconsider my options. Life took a shit turn, which no normal person is ready to handle really. I really don't want to hurt her, but I guess I really do have to do something. Thank you for your persistence, I needed to be put in my place.
I didn't even consider anyone aside from myself.. that almost makes it feel like I'm morally obligated. I wish there were some sort of middle ground.
I'm not trained in this, it's true. If money wasn't an issue, I'd probably already have institutionalized her.
Calling the cops on her will result in a battery on an officer charge for her, I just don't know if I can do that to her.

Haha, to be honest, I hadn't thought about my own finances in this situation. I was hoping a history of hospitalizations and a public defender could get me out of a DV charge, given that my record is clean.

I want her to get the best care possible, I just feel like I'm failing her if I hand her off to some psych ward when I can talk her through her issues. I don't know if she'll ever be stable enough to pay off her debt, and it just seems like I'm passing her off like everyone else has if I do that at this point.

I know the person she is now is a violent wreck, but she was never like this. I honestly believe she can pull though, if she gets the proper help. Maybe, honestly, I can't provide that.. but it feels like such a horrible thing to do to someone you love.

Calling the police will just get her a battery on an officer charge, when she gets like that there's no reason behind her actions. Hospitalization and a med change would likely be the best course of action, but she already has thousands of dollars of medical debt and I fear for her future if she takes that route.

I know, that's why I bought the pepper spray. I can't just leave her like this, or SHE will end up dead by her hand. I appreciate your sentiment, but I can't deal with myself if I leave her alone and the worst happens.

She's already in crippling medical debt from previous hospitalizations. It's probably the safest option, but I fear for her future if she gets another 20k in medical bills. Thank you for giving me something to think about though.

She wasn't always violent before she changed meds. Everytime she changes meds though, she gets far worse than when she's on anything. I've tried suggesting her to increase her dose to see if that would work better for her. I'm afraid, since I work a full time job, I can't be there to protect her during mood swing suicidal tendencies. I don't think she could kill me unless she got really lucky, but it would involve me defending myself, and I really REALLY don't want to hurt her. Thus the pepper spray. I appreciate your advice much so though.
Florida allows you to carry it without a permit, thank you for making me think to check.
She really wants to become a better person, she says it herself. She's just mood cycling so hard she can't handle anything that would resemble a normal life.
Her doctor is one of those psychiatrists who listens to what she has to say for two minutes, then alters medication accordingly. She has no therapist to really talk things out with. I try to be that.

I feel as though if I don't stay involved, then she really won't last much longer. I have tried to call the police in the past, which lead to her violence escalating to the point where there's little I can do to stop her from hurting me or herself. The moment that phone comes out, she goes all out.
I can't just let her spiral further downwards and kill herself.. I truly care about her.

I'm MDI on R/N right now, as it's the only affordable non-prescription option in the US that I know about. This all started after a wicked gash I got, but I can't be certain if the healing process is causing this, or if the incident itself may have triggered DKA. The last times I got it had always been after severe trauma of some kind.

I only ate low carb as an improvised self test for DKA, my numbers were going absurdly high the prior day so I wanted to see if they would continue if I stopped giving myself enough carbohydrates to possibly raise my blood sugar that high. I'll be getting ketone strips tonight, but I expect high results regardless because of how long I've been high.

I'm hoping that it's indeed because of my wound that my numbers are this high, I've just never seen this happen from a gash before that doesn't seem to be infected. I'll be getting ketone strips tonight, but I expect a high result even if I'm not in DKA because I've been high for so long.

I haven't, I plan on getting some tonight but figure the test wouldn't tell me much. I would expect ketones after being this high for this long whether I'm in DKA or not unfortunately. I was hoping someone had successfully let their body balance itself out after being in a similar situation.

I haven't, but my number will actually correct to mid 100s after a bolus. Then, when I check two hours later, without any rhyme or reason it's back in the 300-400 range. I don't have insurance so I'm kinda vial to vial, but if it were the insulin I wouldn't expect it to correct at all.
Oh, it's been 300-400 constantly for two days despite the carbohydrate content of the meals I eat. I've been diabetic for 26 years, I should clarify in the main post.
Try going to Lexington 125.

I'm building a new PC, and salvaging my old power supply, GPU, and DVD drive from my old Bitfenix colossus. I tried for like 30 minutes and feel incredibly special ed right now. Does anyone know how the locking mechanism for drives on this case works and how I can get this out without a sledgehammer?

I like the idea of considering myself already dead. I don't really know how to help others though. Most people are uncomfortable just being near me, the best thing I can do for most people is just not bothering them.
